source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 3 June 1955, p. 7 ("Ulster local government elections: results in county and rural council contests"); Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1955, p. 8 ("Few contests for the county councils"); Irish News, 3 June 1955, p. 1 ("Derry County Council: Coleraine division")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: BNL 3 Jun 1955 p7: 'the only contest was in the Coleraine electoral division ... Mr. D. Hall Christie, C.B.E. ... opposed by a Labour candidate, Alderman J. D. Murphy ... Mr Christie received 1,559 votes and his opponent 621' (OCR garbled); INW 3 Jun 1955 p1 the same.

note: Polled 2 June 1955 (Belfast News-Letter, 3 June 1955: 'Polling took place yesterday in elections for county and rural councils in Northern Ireland'). Coleraine was the only contest; the other eighteen members were returned unopposed, and are named in the Mid-Ulster Mail's report of 21 May 1955 (the Londonderry Sentinel of 19 May 1955 names the same list and the three replacements). Christie was chairman of the county council and a former Mayor of Coleraine; it was the first contest in the division for 50 years. No party label was printed for Christie.
